title: Jewelers and Precious Stone and Metal Workers
description: Design, fabricate, adjust, repair, or appraise jewelry, gold, silver, other precious metals, or gems.

tasks.text: Examine assembled or finished products to ensure conformance to specifications, using magnifying glasses or precision measuring instruments.
Weigh, mix, and melt metal alloys or materials needed for jewelry models.
Create jewelry from materials such as gold, silver, platinum, and precious or semiprecious stones.
Compute costs of labor and materials to determine production costs of products and articles.
Grade stones based on their color, perfection, and quality of cut.
Select and acquire metals and gems for designs.
Determine appraised values of diamonds and other gemstones based on price guides, market fluctuations, and stone grades and rarity.
Create new jewelry designs and modify existing designs, using computers as necessary.
Write or modify design specifications such as the metal contents and weights of items.
Research and analyze reference materials, and consult with interested parties to develop new products or modify existing designs.
Clean and polish metal items and jewelry pieces, using jewelers' tools, polishing wheels, and chemical baths.
Smooth soldered joints and rough spots, using hand files and emery paper, and polish smoothed areas with polishing wheels or buffing wire.
Cut and file pieces of jewelry such as rings, brooches, bracelets, and lockets.
Make repairs, such as enlarging or reducing ring sizes, soldering pieces of jewelry together, and replacing broken clasps and mountings.
Position stones and metal pieces, and set, mount, and secure items in place, using setting and hand tools.
Shape and straighten damaged or twisted articles by hand or using pliers.
Plate articles such as jewelry pieces and watch dials, using silver, gold, nickel, or other metals.
Record the weights and processing times of finished pieces.
Construct preliminary models of wax, metal, clay, or plaster, and form sample castings in molds.
Soften metal to be used in designs by heating it with a gas torch and shape it, using hammers and dies.
Pierce and cut open designs in ornamentation, using hand drills and scroll saws.
Mark, engrave, or emboss designs on metal pieces such as castings, wire, or jewelry, following specifications.
Lay out designs on metal stock, and cut along markings to fabricate pieces used to cast metal molds.
Design and fabricate molds, models, and machine accessories, and modify hand tools used to cast metal and jewelry pieces.
Pour molten metal alloys or other materials into molds to cast models of jewelry.
Cut designs in molds or other materials to be used as models in the fabrication of metal and jewelry products.
Rout out locations where parts are to be joined to items, using routing machines.
Anneal precious metal objects such as coffeepots, tea sets, and trays in gas ovens for prescribed times to soften metal for reworking.
Rotate molds to distribute alloys and to prevent formation of air pockets.
Buy and sell jewelry, or serve as agents between buyers and sellers.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop.

skills.name: Accounting software
skills.def: Software to enable business functions relating to accounting, such as recording transactions or managing budgets. Examples: Intuit QuickBooks.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Computer aided design CAD software
skills.def: Software to design 2D or 3D objects. May include engineering or architectural features. Examples: Computer assisted jewelry design CAD software, Metal designing software.
